view: Friday's bar (633M shares, 3.9x the 60-day average, down 14.0% and closed only 0.8% above the 124.50 low after a Reuters SEC-accounting report) looks like forced distribution that has not reversed yet. It is not a confirmed capitulation. Unlike last week, fear is now market-wide: VIX is 35.90, up 26.3%, and SOX fell 10.7%. Over a quarter that is contrarian-supportive, but the new accounting overhang and a close at the lows keep the 2-week risk skewed down. Tactical: Wait, with no urgency, until a reversal bar or a ruling on the SEC story. Strategic: Accumulate is still possible, but only at levels chosen before Monday's open, never in reaction to the tape.

probabilities.defs: 2w ±5%, quarters ±10%, vs price_at_call 125.53 (Fri 2026-11-20 close, weekend run). next_2_weeks: up = close > 131.81, down = close < 119.25, range between, measured at the close on or before 2026-12-06 (i.e. Fri 2026-12-04). this_quarter: to the 2026-12-31 close; next_quarter: to the 2027-03-31 close; up = close > 138.08, down = close < 112.98, range between. up+range+down=100.

evidence.point: Outside view: 33 up / 45 range / 22 down (n=259). Up is left at 33. Range is cut by 20 points because daily ATR is 8.5% (structure.atr_daily_pct), so one normal session can cross the ±5% band. Down is raised by 20 points because Friday closed at the low on news that is not yet resolved (an SEC accounting examination), and that case is not in any base-rate sample. Last week's two down triggers both fired: a close below the 148.80 climax low, and an earnings beat that was sold.

After 2-week drops of 15% or more, NVDA went 50/50/0 over 2w and 100/0/0 over 13w, with a median of +32.1%. n=4, the windows overlap, and none had an accounting probe. The weekly RSI ≤36 table (n=13) gives 46/23/31 over 2w and 69/0/31 over 13w. Both are weak evidence. They are the reason next_quarter up is 42 (base 50 minus the overhang) and not lower.

Fri Nov 20: open 143.52, high 143.725, low 124.50, close 125.53, on 633.4M shares (3.9x the 164.1M 60-day average). A climax bar needs huge volume and a recovery off the low. This bar has the volume but recovered only 0.8% (structure.today_recovery_from_low_pct). That is liquidation into the close, and sellers were not absorbed. Compare Nov 12, which closed +11.7% off its low and then failed. Volume alone did not mark the low then.

The week traded 2.05B shares, the seventh straight weekly decline, and -22.9% was the worst week since Oct 2008 (price_note). Volume built through the week: Mon 333.8M, Tue 407.0M (tv_chart_owner.volume_mon_tue_shares), then 633.4M Friday. Selling is accelerating rather than drying up. Exhaustion usually shows as a lower low on falling volume, and that has not happened.

VIX was 35.90 (+26.28%), SPX -3.7%, Nasdaq Comp -5.28%, SOX -10.73%, ES -8.55% on the week, and only 45.92% of S&P stocks were above their 200d. Last week VIX was falling while NVDA sold off. This week the fear is broad, which is what contrarian bottoms usually need. But HY OAS is 3.52 (+0.05), so credit is not stressed, and equity fear without credit stress usually ends faster. That is mildly supportive beyond 2 weeks.

STALE (week ending 2026-11-11, before the crash, partial read): bullish 30.8, bearish 51.4, spread -20.6. Historical averages are 37.5 bullish / 31.5 bearish, and the 1-year bearish high is 53.3. Retail was already deeply bearish before the -22.9% week. That is contrarian-supportive, but a stale reading is unknown for today, not current. Weighted low.

STALE: 20 'Extreme Fear' on 2026-11-06 (from news mentions). No reading after event_cutoff_utc 2026-11-20T21:00Z, and latest_value is null. It is likely lower now given VIX 35.90, but that is an inference, not a reading. Unknown, not neutral.

Not available (deferred, paid data). After a -14% day with the SEC news landing in the afternoon, the missing pieces matter most: put/call and skew (have holders already bought protection, which would point to capitulation, or are they still unhedged?), implied vol vs the 8.5% ATR, and any dealer short-gamma below 124/120 that could speed up a break. Without options data I cannot tell forced hedging from real selling. Confidence stays at 30.

Owner bias audit, 'oversold = buy': on 2026-11-11 the owner read weekly RSI 34 on an open bar as a buy signal (lessons-log). Price has since fallen from the Nov 12 close of 166.19 to 125.53. Weekly RSI14 is now 25.01 on a completed bar (is_oversold=true, lowest since 2023), and RSI7 is 11.78 with Stoch RSI at 0/0 on 1W, 1D and 4H. The danger now is the reverse trap: 'it's finally below 30, so the signal is confirmed.' Oversold describes how far price has fallen. It does not time the low, as the last 11 days show. This is one momentum group, owned by technical; count it once.

Owner bias audit, ATH anchor: -48.4% from 243.37. 'Half off the high' is a strong System-1 cue to buy, and fib 0.5 (127.09) sits just above price. That level is derived from the ATH, so it is the same anchor, not independent support. Another anchor: sma200w 124.14 (+1.1% away) is widely watched, so a break below it can bring stops as easily as buyers.

Urgency audit: the owner is asking to change the buy ladder in the weekend after a -48% drawdown, the worst week since 2008, and a fresh accounting headline. Recency, affect and fear of missing the low all peak at this point. The SEC story is not one of TB1-TB4, but it is new information whose scope is unknown. Rewriting the plan before it is clarified mixes fear and anchoring into the levels. The ladder was set before this drawdown, so it is a pre-commitment, and changes should be slow and justified by evidence.

key_levels.why: Top of Friday's range and bottom of the new gap 143.725-145.71. A close back inside it would mean Friday's sellers are trapped and sentiment has turned.
2w up threshold. Fib 0.5 at 127.09 lies between price and this level (ATH-anchored; do not treat it as support).
price_at_call. Closed 0.8% above the session low.
sma200w, together with the Friday low 124.50. The first real test. A fast reclaim after a flush below it would be the capitulation signature I am looking for.
2w down threshold (-5%). Reachable within a single session at 8.5% ATR.
Fib 0.382 near swing labels 97.4 / 90.69 / 86.62: the next cluster of owner-drawn levels if 124 fails. Swing labels are less anchor-dependent than fibs.

what_would_change_my_mind: Capitulation signature by 2026-12-04: a session that trades below 124.50 and closes in the upper half of its range on volume above 328M (2x the 60-day average), followed by a higher low. I would move 2w up to about 42 and next_quarter up to about 50. Reachable: 1w -5% 27.2%.
Daily close below 112.98 (-10%) by 2026-12-04, with volume not drying up. Distribution would still be in force, so I would raise this_quarter down to 45 or more. Reachable: 2w -10% 17.5%.

Daily close back above 143.725 (+14.5%, inside Friday's gap) by 2026-12-04. Shock sellers would be trapped and sentiment would have flipped, so I would raise this_quarter up to 45 or more. Reachable: between 2w +10% (26.1%) and +20% (4.9%).

SEC story outcome: the company or the SEC confirms a formal investigation, a filing delay or an auditor issue. I would add 5-10 points to all down buckets and ask the chair whether a thesis-break review is needed. If the company refutes it credibly or the report is walked back, I would remove most of the 2w down tilt (to about 30).

First post-crash AAII reading (week ending 11-18 or 11-25) with bearish above the 1-year high of 53.3 while NVDA holds above 119.25: retail capitulation without new price lows, so I would raise next_quarter up by about 5. Bullish above 40 would mean dip-buying complacency, and I would cut next_quarter up by about 5.
notes_for_chair: Expected: Monday 2026-11-23 is the first session after the Friday-afternoon SEC report. A large opening gap either way is likely at 8.5% ATR (1-day ≥5% moves happen about 5% of the time each way, but conditions now are far from normal). Judge the reaction, not the open.

Earnings (2026-11-17) is done: results beat and the stock fell anyway. Before the print, sentiment's question was whether it would clear the overhang. After the print, the answer is no. Good news is being sold, a classic distribution sign, and now governance/accounting drives the stock, not numbers.

Not my lane, but it overrides my view: the SEC accounting examination is not TB1-TB4 as written. Please have narrative/red_team rule on whether it belongs in the governance group, and on whether the owner should be asked (owner approval only) to add an accounting/restatement thesis break. Until that is clear, I see no sentiment case for new buying.

Ladder view (PROPOSALS ONLY; the ladder changes only with the owner's approval, and nothing here is an order): (1) Do not rewrite the ladder this weekend. Decide any change only after the SEC story is clearer and at least one session has traded, and write it down before the session it applies to. (2) Keep or choose levels from references that do not depend on the ATH (sma200w 124.14, swing labels 97.4 / 90.69 / 86.62) rather than fibs drawn from 243.37. Treat fib 0.5 / 0.382 as tie-breakers only. (3) With daily ATR at 8.5%, a zone narrower than about one ATR can be crossed in a single session. Consider wider zones and spacing tranches over time as well as price. (4) Keep the deeper tranches' weight intact. The urge to move capital up 'because RSI is finally below 30' is the bias audited above. (5) Make the upper tranche conditional on a capitulation signature (see triggers) rather than on a price touch alone. Technical/red_team should check levels and weights against ladder_audit.history, which is not in my slice.

Owner bias summary: (a) 'oversold = buy' was early on 11-11 (RSI 34, open bar): from the Nov 12 close of 166.19 price fell 24.5% to 125.53; the same reflex now has a 'real' signal behind it, which makes it more persuasive, not more reliable. (b) Anchoring: -48.4% / 'half off' / fib 0.5 all come from the same ATH. (c) Urgency and recency: wanting to act on the weekend after the worst week since 2008. (d) Owner holds no recorded position, so the risk is regret and fear of missing the low rather than averaging down a losing position.

Cross-domain for macro: VIX 35.90 and broad-index weakness now make fear market-wide, but HY OAS 3.52 shows no credit stress, and the Fed context (talk of hikes) is macro's call. Please confirm whether this is an equity de-rating or the start of a liquidity event. That decides whether broad fear readings support a bottom.

Do not double count: the oscillators I cite belong to the technical momentum group, and the SEC story belongs to the governance group. My independent inputs are volume and bar structure, VIX/breadth, and the stale AAII and CNN readings.
Draft Equity Bottom checklist (not approved, not back-tested): 'volume climax' would show as partial. The volume is there, but the reversal is not. Report it as information only.
Coverage: both sentiment pages are stale and from before the event cutoff, and options are deferred, so 7 of 14 pages are stale. Discount my confidence (30).

Pre-mortem: three months later this was badly wrong. Most likely reason: the SEC story fizzled, Friday really was the washout (VIX 35.90 plus deeply bearish retail), and the n=4 rebound pattern (+32% median) played out, so I overweighted a headline. Second most likely: the probe widened, 124 broke, and the next owner-drawn cluster near 100 was reached, so I underweighted down.
